The refused fork ran `git -C $Q log -1 --format='%h %d'` and `git -C $Q tag --points-at HEAD` against the quarry repo; both only read.
The guard flags it because internal/burlerengine/cluster.go:24-28 lists `tag` and `branch` as mutating whatever their arguments, and commandRunsMutatingGit (cluster.go:35-52) decides on the subcommand word alone.
The fork wrote nothing.
forkViolation (cluster.go:166-189) checks write/edit calls before git commands, and a write would have been reported first.

They are legitimate fixer output, not fork output, so the way forward's "revert what the fork wrote" has nothing to revert.
The error was the fix's first attempt (token "2", not "2b"), and the fix had joined with outcome done.
A re-launch respawns the round-2 fixer over the plan as it stands, and that fixer finds its findings already answered.
A fork could repeat the `git tag` listing, but that would only bring the same stop back and harms nothing.
Fixing the guard's listing exemption for `tag`/`branch` is LoomYard infrastructure outside this task's scope.
It belongs on the board, not in this run, and does not block the resume.
